stories.title: Guangzhou 2018 · Passage A
stories.topic: 2018 A 篇｜改变人生的生日礼物
paragraphs: For his eleventh birthday, Lin was given a gift that would shape his life.
林在十一岁生日那天收到了一份改变他一生的礼物。
On that day his father took him to the Children’s Activity Centre and said he could choose any course that interested him.
爸爸带他去儿童活动中心，说他可以选任何一门自己感兴趣的课。
There was just one requirement: Lin would have to promise to study it for at least one year.
唯一的要求是，林必须答应至少学一年。
To that point Lin had had many hobbies, but none kept his interest for more than a week or two.
在那之前，林有过不少爱好，可没有一个能让他感兴趣超过一两周。
His mum once gave him a bag of stamps to encourage stamp collecting.
妈妈曾送给他一袋邮票，鼓励他集邮。
That hobby lasted a week.
这个爱好只持续了一周。
Then his father got him some paints hoping that Lin's artistic side would shine through.
后来，爸爸买来一些颜料，希望林能展露艺术天分。
Those paints were now under his bed, still unopened.
那些颜料现在还在床底下，包装都没拆。
This time Lin’s parents would let him decide.
这一次，父母让他自己选。
Lin's eyes moved down the noticeboard that listed all the courses on offer.
林沿着公告板一项项看活动中心开设的课程，
He stopped at "Photography".
在“摄影”一栏停了下来。
He liked the idea of taking beautiful pictures but the notice said that each student needed their own camera.
他喜欢拍漂亮照片的想法，可通知上说每名学生都得自备相机。
Although Lin's family weren't poor, they weren’t rich either, and a camera cost a lot of money.
林家不穷，也谈不上富裕，而相机价格不菲。
He continued looking.
他继续往下看。
The next course to catch his eye was "Language Art".
接着吸引他的是“语言艺术”。
He didn’t even know what that meant.
他甚至不知道那是什么意思。
His father explained that it taught people how to make public speeches.
爸爸解释说，这门课教人如何当众演讲。
Lin, a shy boy, could think of nothing worse.
林很害羞，在他看来，没有比这更糟的事了。
Then he saw it.
这时他看到了“烹饪”。
"Cooking" sounded like something he'd like to do.
这听起来像是他喜欢做的事。
It was inexpensive and convenient, it could be done alone and it was also creative.
学起来花钱不多，也方便，可以一个人做，还能发挥创意。
Based on Lin’s hobby history, his dad had doubts, but he agreed.
想到林过去那些爱好，爸爸有些犹豫，最后还是同意了。
Much to his parents' surprise, Lin kept his promise.
让父母意外的是，林守住了承诺。
He studied cooking at the Centre every Saturday, and practised at home, making delicious meals for his family.
他每周六去活动中心学烹饪，还在家练习，给家人做可口的饭菜。
Everyone looked forward to birthdays, when they could eat his cakes.
大家都盼着过生日，因为那时就能吃到他做的蛋糕。
Lin got great satisfaction from the pleasure his food brought to others.
看到自己做的食物能让别人开心，林觉得非常满足。
The months turned to years but his hobby never changed again.
几个月变成了几年，他的爱好一直没变。
Now Lin is an adult and runs a successful restaurant.
如今，林已长大，经营着一家生意很好的餐馆。
When customers say they enjoy his meal, he still gets the same pleasure he did as a child, and remembers the special gift he received all those years ago.
客人说喜欢他做的饭菜时，他依然能体会到小时候的那种快乐，也会想起多年前收到的那份特别的生日礼物。

stories.title: Guangzhou 2018 · Passage B
stories.topic: 2018 B 篇｜餐馆是怎么发展起来的
paragraphs: Experts believe that there are more than 8 million restaurants in the world today.
专家认为，如今世界上的餐馆超过八百万家。
So it might surprise you to learn that restaurants, as we know them, have only existed for a few centuries.
你可能想不到，我们今天所说的餐馆其实只有几百年的历史。
Before 1765, there were no restaurants.
1765年以前，没有
That is, there were no places that provided the restaurant experience.
能提供现代餐馆体验的地方。
There was nowhere in which a waiter brought you food and drink that you picked from a menu.
你找不到一家店，可以先从菜单上选吃的喝的，再让服务员端上来。
In fact, there were no menus anywhere.
那时甚至根本没有菜单。
There were eating places travellers could go to centuries before that.
在那之前的几百年里，旅人也有地方吃东西。
The countryside was full of inns that would serve food.
乡间到处是供应饭菜的旅店，
And there were taverns where one could get drinks.
也有能喝酒的酒馆。
The rich could also eat special meals prepared by private cooks.
富人还可以请私人厨师做讲究的饭菜。
But none of them could be called a “restaurant”.
不过，这些地方都称不上“餐馆”。
A man called Boulanger changed that.
一个叫布朗热的人改变了这种情况。
In 1765, he opened a place in Paris that sold soups（汤）.
1765年，他在巴黎开了一家店卖汤。
On his sign he used the word "restaurant" to describe what he was selling.
招牌上，他用“restaurant”这个词来形容自己卖的东西。
At that time, soups were considered something that could help "restore"（恢复）your health- in French the word "restore" is “restaurer”--- so he called the soups "restaurants".
当时人们认为喝汤能帮助恢复健康，而法语里“恢复”是 restaurer，于是他把这些汤叫作“restaurants”。
Soon, people started buying Boulanger's soups even when they were not ill.
很快，人们即使没生病也去买他的汤。
And over time, people began to use the word "restaurant" to refer to a place selling soup rather than the soup itself.
渐渐地，“restaurant”转而指卖汤的地方。
More "restaurants" opened in France, and people began to buy soups more often.
法国开了更多这样的店，人们也更常买汤喝。
Later, restaurants in Paris began to serve other food besides soup.
后来，巴黎的餐馆除了汤也开始供应别的食物。
In the 1790s, menus started to appear.
18世纪90年代，菜单开始出现。
By the mid-1800s, there were many types of restaurants throughout the world.
到19世纪中叶，各类餐馆已经遍布世界各地。
The United States offered coffee shops.
美国有咖啡馆，
Tea houses became popular throughout China.
中国各地流行茶馆。
Paris created beautiful restaurants for the rich.
巴黎开起了招待富人的漂亮餐馆。
The British began to copy the French, and the restaurant idea spread throughout the British Empire.
英国人也开始效仿法国人，开餐馆的做法随之传遍大英帝国。
Today cities are filled with all types of restaurants.
如今，城市里到处都是各式各样的餐馆，
Diners have millions of options from which to choose.
食客有数不清的选择。

stories.title: Guangzhou 2018 · Passage C
paragraphs: Many people know that rubbish is a big problem on planet Earth.
许多人知道垃圾是地球上的一个大问题。
What many people don't know is that junk（垃圾）has become a problem in outer space too.
很多人还不知道，垃圾在外太空也成了问题。
According to BBC News, there are more than 22,000 pieces of space junk floating around the earth.
据英国广播公司新闻报道，有两万两千多件太空垃圾在绕地球漂浮。
And these are just the things that we can see from the surface of the earth by telescopes（望远镜）.
这些还只是我们在地面上用望远镜能看到的。
There are also millions of smaller pieces of junk that we can't see.
另有数百万块更小的碎片，我们看不见。

Objects, like bits of old space rockets or satellites, move around the planet at very high speeds, so fast that even a very small piece can break important satellites or become dangerous to astronauts.
旧火箭和卫星的碎片等物体高速绕地球飞行。即使是很小的一块，也会撞坏重要的卫星，或者给宇航员带来危险。
If the tiniest piece of junk crashed into a spaceship, it could damage the vehicle.
哪怕最小的碎片撞上飞船，也可能损坏飞船。
To make things worse, when two objects in space crash, they break into many smaller pieces.
更糟的是，两个物体在太空相撞后，会碎成更多小块。
For example, when a U. S. satellite hit an old Russian rocket in 2009, it broke into more than 2,000 pieces, increasing the amount of space junk.
例如，2009年美国一颗卫星撞上一枚俄罗斯旧火箭，产生了两千多块碎片，进一步增加了太空垃圾的数量。
To reduce additional space junk, countries have agreed that all new space tools can only stay in space for 25 years at most.
为了减少新增垃圾，各国约定，新发射的航天设备在太空中最多只能停留25年。
Each tool must be built to fall safely into the earth's atmosphere after that time.
设计时，就必须让设备在期满后能安全落回地球大气层，
In the upper parts of the atmosphere, it will burn up.
并在大气层上部烧毁。
Many scientists are also suggesting different ways to clean up space junk.
许多科学家也在提出不同的清理办法。
In England scientists are testing a metal net that can be fired into space junk.
英国科学家正在测试一种可以朝太空垃圾发射的金属网。
The net catches the junk and then pulls it into the earth's atmosphere to burn up.
网住垃圾后，就把它拉进地球大气层烧掉。
The Germans are building robots that can collect pieces of space junk and bring them back to Earth to be safely destroyed.
德国人正在制造能收集太空垃圾的机器人，把碎片带回地球安全销毁。
“The problem is becoming more challenging because we're sending more objects into space to help people use their mobile phones and computers,” says Marco Castronuovo, an Italian space researcher.
意大利太空研究人员马尔科·卡斯特罗努沃说：“为了方便人们使用手机和电脑，我们正在往太空送去更多物体，所以这个问题越来越难解决。”
“The time to act is now.
他说：“现在就该行动。
The longer we leave the problem, the bigger it will become,” he says.
拖得越久，问题就越大。”

stories.title: Guangzhou 2017 · Passage A
paragraphs: We often hear stories of animals rescuing people.
我们常听说动物救人的故事。
But now someone has managed to return the favour.
如今，有人也救了一只动物，算是回报了这份恩情。
The event took place one snowy January morning.
这件事发生在一月一个下雪的早晨。
Thomas Smith was walking his dog, Jack, in the park.
托马斯·史密斯正在公园遛他的狗杰克。
"As I was walking, I just saw Jack running onto the ice towards the ducks in the middle, and then he fell into the water and couldn't climb out," said Smith.
“我走着走着，就看见杰克跑上冰面，朝湖中央的鸭子奔去。接着它掉进水里，怎么也爬不出来。”史密斯说。
He realized he had no choice but to try and save his dog.
他意识到自己只能下水救狗。
"Someone else told me the lake was only one-metre deep, but it was at least twice that.
“有人告诉我湖水只有一米深，其实至少有两米。
I had to break my way through the 6-cm ice.
我得一路破开六厘米厚的冰。
Finally, I got Jack by the neck and pulled him out.
最后，我抓住杰克的脖子，把它拉了出来。
I don't think I've ever felt so cold by the time we got back to dry land.
等我们回到岸上时，我觉得自己从来没这么冷过。
And when we got there, everyone was asking if Jack was okay — no one was particularly worried about me! "
可一上岸，大家都在问杰克有没有事，没谁特别担心我！”
A neighbour, Julie Brown, saw it all happen.
邻居朱莉·布朗目睹了全过程。
"The dog went onto an icy lake.
“那只狗跑到结冰的湖上，
All of a sudden, it started to go under.
突然就开始往下沉。
There were crowds of people around, and they were all shouting and screaming.
周围围着很多人，大家都在叫喊。
Before I knew it, the owner (Smith) was in the water forcing his way through the ice.
我还没反应过来，主人史密斯已经下了水，破冰往前。
I can't begin to imagine how cold it was.
水有多冷，我简直不敢想。
Everyone was very nervous, but he was as cool as a cucumber — he just crawled back out, put the dog on its lead, and went home. "
大家都紧张极了，他却镇定自若。他就那样爬上来，给狗拴好牵引绳，然后回家了。”
Many regard him as a hero, but Mr. Smith is quite laid-back about it.
许多人把史密斯先生视为英雄，他自己却看得很淡。
"Most dog owners are the same as me.
“大多数养狗的人都跟我一样，
They would do what I did without a second thought.
会毫不犹豫地这么做。
But in the future, I'm going to make sure he's on a lead near any icy ponds. "
不过以后只要靠近结冰的池塘，我一定会给它拴好牵引绳。”
Pets are members of our family.
宠物是家里的一员。
Would you do the same for them?
你也会为它们这么做吗？

stories.title: Guangzhou 2017 · Passage B
paragraphs: Tim Berners-Lee is not the most famous inventor in the world.
蒂姆·伯纳斯-李并非世界上最有名的发明家。
However, his invention has changed our lives.
他的发明却改变了我们的生活。
He was born in London, England in 1955.
他于1955年出生在英国伦敦。
When he was a small boy, Tim was interested in playing with electrical things.
蒂姆小时候就喜欢摆弄电器。
He studied science at Oxford University.
他在牛津大学学习科学，
He made his first computer from an old television at the age of 21.
21岁时用一台旧电视机做出了自己的第一台电脑。
Tim started working on early computers.
蒂姆开始研究早期的电脑。
At that time, they were much bigger than now.
那时的电脑比现在大得多。
He worked in England then Switzerland.
他先在英国工作，后来去了瑞士。
Tim was really interested in two things, computers and how the brain works.
蒂姆对两件事很感兴趣：电脑和大脑的工作原理。
How could the brain connect so many facts so quickly?
大脑怎么能那么快地把这么多信息联系起来呢？
He had to work with people all over the world.
他得和世界各地的人合作，
They shared information about computers.
交流有关电脑的信息。
It was hard to manage all the information.
整理这些信息很难，
He answered the same questions again and again.
他一遍遍回答同样的问题，
It took a lot of time.
花了很多时间。
It was even difficult for computers in the same office in Switzerland to share information.
在瑞士，就连同一间办公室里的电脑也很难共享信息。
Tim also forgot things easily.
蒂姆自己也容易忘事。
Could a computer work like a brain?
电脑能像大脑一样工作吗？
Could it "talk" to other computers?
电脑之间能互相“说话”吗？
There was an Internet already but it was difficult to use.
当时已经有了互联网，却很难使用。
In 1989, Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web (WWW) all by himself.
1989年，蒂姆·伯纳斯-李独自发明了万维网（WWW）。
This had a special language that helped computers talk to each other on the Internet.
它有一种特殊的语言，让电脑能在互联网上彼此通信。
When people wanted to share information with others, they used the World Wide Web.
人们想和别人分享信息时，就使用万维网。
The Internet grew quickly after that.
此后互联网很快发展起来。
Tim Berners-Lee doesn't think he did anything special.
蒂姆·伯纳斯-李觉得自己没有做什么特别的事。
He says that all of the ideas about the Internet were already there.
他说，有关互联网的点子早就有了，
All he did was to put them together.
自己只是把它们组合起来。
He says that many other people worked together to make the Internet what it is today.
还有许多人共同努力，才有了今天的互联网。
Most inventors want to become rich.
多数发明家希望发财，
But Tim gave away the World Wide Web for nothing.
蒂姆却把万维网无偿地分享给了大家。
He now works in America.
他现在在美国工作，
He helps people share technology and wants the Internet to be free for everyone to use.
帮助人们共享技术，也希望人人都能免费使用互联网。
Maybe he is the most important but least famous inventor in the world today!
也许他就是当今世界上最重要、却最不出名的发明家！

stories.title: Libraries
paragraphs: Public Libraries
公共图书馆
Most towns in Britain have a public library.
英国大多数城镇都有公共图书馆。
A library usually has a large selection of books and other resources, which library members can use and borrow for free.
图书馆通常有大量图书和其他资源，持证读者可以免费使用和借阅。
Britain's First Public Library
英国第一家公共图书馆
The first public library in Britain opened in Manchester in 1852.
英国第一家公共图书馆于1852年在曼彻斯特开放。
Its first librarian was a man called Edward Edwards.
首任图书管理员名叫爱德华·爱德华兹。
Edwards attended the library's opening ceremony and two famous writers called Charles Dickens and William Thackeray were there too.
他出席了开馆仪式，两位著名作家查尔斯·狄更斯和威廉·萨克雷也到场了。
How to Join a Library
如何办理借书证
To join a library, go to your local library and fill in a form.
到当地的图书馆填一张表，
You'll receive a library card which is needed when using library services.
你就能领到借书证。使用图书馆服务时需要出示这张卡。
Library Services
图书馆服务
Modern public libraries have something for everyone.
现代公共图书馆能满足不同读者的需求。
Most of them have audio books, CDs, newspapers and DVDs as well as books to borrow.
除了书，大多数馆还提供有声书、CD、报纸和DVD供人借阅。
Mobile Libraries
流动图书馆
Not everyone can get to a library.
并不是每个人都能去图书馆。
Some people live far away from towns and cities.
有些人住得离城镇很远，
Other people find it difficult to go out because they have an illness or a disability.
还有些人因为生病或身体有障碍，出门不方便。
Thanks to mobile libraries, these people can still borrow books.
多亏有流动图书馆，他们也能借到书。
Unlike most libraries, which store books in buildings, mobile libraries usually keep their books in a mini-bus.
多数图书馆把书存放在建筑里，流动图书馆则通常把书放在一辆小型巴士里。
The back of the mini-bus has shelves for the books, and it is big enough for borrowers to step inside and look around.
巴士后部装有书架，空间足以让读者上车浏览。
A driver takes the mini-bus to a certain place at a certain time, so people know when to expect it.
司机定时把车开到指定地点，大家知道什么时候来，
They can then return their books and borrow some more.
就可以还书，再借几本。
All Aboard the Library!
上车看书！
A school in London didn't have space for a library inside the building.
伦敦有一所学校，教学楼内腾不出地方建图书馆，
However, everybody agreed that it was still important to have a school library.
可大家都认为学校有图书馆很重要。
So, the head of the school, Graham Blake, decided to park an old bus on the school car park and change it into a library.
于是，校长格雷厄姆·布莱克决定把一辆旧巴士停在学校停车场，改成图书馆。
Pupils helped to paint the bus, and after eight months, the new library was ready.
学生们帮忙给车刷漆，八个月后，新图书馆就准备好了。

stories.title: Guangzhou 2017 · Passage D
paragraphs: People can't see you when you're speaking on the phone, but they can hear you.
打电话时，对方看不见你，却能听见你。
So, the way you speak is especially important.
你说话的方式因此特别重要。
In fact, researchers have calculated that 80% of communication over the phone is through your tone of voice; and only 20% is from the words you use.
研究人员算出，电话交流中的信息有80%通过语气传递，只有20%来自你所用的词语。
Here are our top tips on how to speak over the phone.
下面是一些打电话时的实用建议。
1. Facial Expressions
1. 面部表情
Your facial expression can influence your voice.
表情会影响声音。
For example, if you smile, your voice will sound warm and friendly, just the opposite, if you have an angry look on your face, it can make you sound unpleasant.
微笑时，你的声音听起来会温暖友好。皱着脸生气时，说话的声音可能就不太好听。
2. Volume
2. 音量
If you speak too loudly, you could sound angry.
声音太大，听起来像在生气。
And if you speak too softly, it'll be difficult to hear you.
声音太轻，对方又听不清。
So, speak loudly enough to be heard clearly, but not so loud that you're shouting.
音量以能让人听清为宜，别大到像在喊叫。
3. Pace
3. 语速
The pace of your voice is how quickly you speak.
语速是指你说话的快慢，
And this can show how you feel.
也能反映情绪。
For example, an angry person might speak faster than normal.
生气的人可能比平常说得快，
Or a downhearted person might speak very slowly.
情绪低落的人可能说得很慢。
Try speaking a little more slowly than normal.
试着比平常说慢一点。
This will make you sound confident, and it'll make it easier for the other person to understand you.
这样听起来更自信，对方也更容易听懂。
4. Gestures
4. 手势
Gesturing can influence the tone of your voice.
做手势会影响语气。
When you gesture, you bring more air into the lungs, which can make your voice sound warmer.
打手势时，你吸进肺里的空气更多，声音听起来会更温暖。
Gestures are also useful to help you stress the right words or even find the words you need.
手势也有助于强调该强调的词，甚至能帮你想起要说的词。
The best thing about gesturing during a phone call is that no one can see what you're doing, so you can gesture as wildly as you like!
打电话做手势的好处是没人看得见，你想怎么比画都行！
5. Movement
5. 走动
If you're feeling nervous, stand up and move around.
如果你感到紧张，就站起来走一走。
It will reduce the nervousness in your body and help your voice to sound more confident.
这能缓解身体的紧张，也能让你的声音听起来更自信。
6. Pauses
6. 停顿
Using pauses every now and then can help you to slow down.
偶尔停一停有助于放慢语速，
This will make you sound more confident and in control.
听起来更自信、更从容。
Also, if you pause after giving some new information, it'll give the other person time to understand it.
告诉对方新信息后稍作停顿，也能给对方一点时间去理解。
At the same time, listen to how the other person uses pauses.
同时，留意对方如何停顿。
They could tell you something about the speaker's feeling.
这可能让你听出对方的情绪。
For example, when a speaker is really angry, he might use pauses and says, "I... am... so... angry..."
例如，非常生气的人可能会一字一顿地说：“我……真的……太……生气了……”
